Fibber rolls are also made of similar material as used in erosion control blankets but are rolled into large diameter logs. Coir type logs/ Logs made of rice/wheat straw also may be used. These logs are nailed into the slope to slow down the surface water. Tensar type geo-grids also may be effective. column1: - d. The ratio of mass of the foundation to mass of the GT and ST plant shall be at least 2.

To reduce the risk of dynamic compaction the maximum load on any pile supporting a GT and ST foundation shall not exceed 60 per cent of its working capacity during the normal operating conditions and shall not exceed 90 per cent in extreme conditions. For a foundation supported by soil the same limits apply to the allowable bearing capacity of the soil.

- f. The design  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundations  shall  include  the  thermal  effects  on  the foundation and its ability to withstand the extreme differential temperatures likely to be experienced by the foundation, during the construction as well as throughout its design life. Protective measures during construction shall be part of the design.

- g. The section  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundation  below  ground  shall  be  protected  with  a coating system to resist attack from the sulphate content in the soils and chlorides from the ground water. Further protection against corrosion of the reinforcement (which leads to expansion of the concrete and cracking) due to the severe chloride ion content of the soils and groundwater shall be provided as covered by the concrete section of this Specification.
- h. The GT and ST foundation shall be poured in one operation and construction joints are not permitted unless in exceptional circumstances and with the approval of the Owner/Owner's Engineer.

- i. The design, detailing and construction of the GT and ST foundations shall allow fully for  the  'buildability'  of  the  foundations,  particularly  where  congested  areas  of reinforcement are required.

- j. In addition to the static structural design the contractor shall prove the design of the turbine  supporting  structure  dynamically  by  modelling  the  bearing  points,  the foundation and the soil body together, taking the full consideration of the coupling effect and interaction between the three systems.

- k. The  design  of  turbine  supporting  structures,  if  applicable,  shall  be  same  as  that supporting the gas turbines except in some designs a table top structure and columns are erected over a mat foundation. The supporting structure if cast monolithically shall  be  analysed  with  due  consideration  of  the  flexibility  of  each  structural component.  If the table top structure is supported by springs the substructure may be  designed  as  a  static  structure  if  its  superstructure  proves  a  sufficient  isolation achieved by the springs.

column1: A surface water drainage system shall be provided for the Plant. The design shall allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water over the whole of the Site (arising from run-off of natural water from buildings, roads, ground surface, paved areas, etc.). All buildings shall be provided with roof drainage for disposal of surface water, and be connected to the surface water drainage system. The surface water drainage system shall be arranged and designed to effectively manage all run-off and discharge arising from the Site.
The Storm  water  Drainage  system  shall  be  designed  considering  100  years  rainfall  return  period  and rainfall intensity equal to the retention period.

Basements, cable and pipe trenches and tunnels shall be constructed with adequate provision for drainage. Floors to basements, trenches and tunnels shall be laid to falls and/or drainage channels provided therein. Any water entering the basements trenches or tunnels shall be routed to sumps and connected to the surface water drainage system. Where connection to the surface water drainage system is not practical, then provision to pump-out water from the trench or tunnel drainage sump, by permanent and/or portable sump pumps shall be made. Fire deluge water shall be gathered into storm water catch pits and discharged via main storm water system and prevented from entering tunnels.
Primary site drainage and sub-soil drainage shall be provided, where necessary, on external areas generally to protect the site from run off into building areas etc.

Storm water drainage sumps, pumps and electrical equipment shall be located to avoid hazardous areas. If unavoidable then the pumps and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements in accordance with API and NFPA for operation in hazardous environments. Pumps shall be able to be withdrawn from the sump at surface level for maintenance and repair. The sump and valve chamber shall be equipped with access covers and ladders for maintenance purposes. The sump chamber shall be designed hydraulically so as not to impair pump performance.

column1: Note that the depth of the capillary rise zone shall be taken as 1.5 m above the highest ground water level (considering seasonal variation) for underground facility design and construction. Sulphate and chloride levels shall be determined by the Contractor's soil investigation.
Bitumastic paint shall be applied on top of all blinding concrete if recommended by Geotech report except where horizontal shear resistance is required.
Embedded  materials  shall  be  accurately  fabricated  and  assembled  to  suit  the  construction  interface required.

All steel embedment in concrete shall be accurately positioned and securely anchored either directly to the formwork or by templates prior to pouring the concrete. Pockets for later insertion of assemblies generally will be allowed.
Embedment shall be clean both before they are installed and after placement of the concrete.

Where embedment are required for major equipment items e.g. Turbine Generator, Pump Foundations, etc, then anchor bolts, attachments and embedment shall be located and secured prior to concrete placement with accurately made steel templates. In the above cases tolerances shall be as specified by the equipment manufacturer . Templates shall be interconnected and braced with steel members that maintain the anchor bolt alignment and position.
However, penetrating type of bolts are accepted if recommended by OEM.
Welding of embedment, to the reinforcement cage to secure their location, will not be accepted.
Corrosion protection shall be provided to all embedment, suitable to the environment in which they are cast. Generally, the following exposure conditions shall be considered as a minimum:
- Dry internal environments
- Wet internal environments
- External environments not exposed to seawater or seawater spray
- External environments exposed to seawater spray/splash zone

column1: The  necessity  of  welding  plant  fixings  etc.  to  embedment  exposed  at  the  concrete  surface  in  exposed environments shall be considered at design stage and wherever possible alternative fixing details shall be provided in order to preserve the original corrosion protective coatings.

Where this detail cannot be designed out then to protect the embedded item(s) from corrosion, for the life of the station, the following minimum material requirements and corrosion protection criteria shall be provided.
- All anchor bolts shall have a concrete cover of at least 100 mm.

The  corrosion  protection  system  provided  to  concrete  embedment  shall  also  consider  the  corrosion protection system(s) provided to adjacent plant and the dual requirements shall be considered collectively, where applicable, to select the most appropriate solution.
Concrete construction tolerances shall comply with ACI 117.

The minimum lateral distance between adjacent individual spread footings bearing at the same grade on soil shall be B/2, where B is the footing width or diameter of the larger footing. For Square or rectangular footings, of width B, the minimum lateral separation distance should be no less than B.  Where the lateral spacing  is  less  than  recommended,  the  stress  distribution  between  the  adjacent  footings  should  be analysed.

Net design bearing capacities and settlement estimates for tanks shall be based on the assumption that the foundation soils underlying the tank are not significantly affected by adjacent tanks. The lateral distance between adjacent tanks should be limited to a distance B, where B is the diameter of the smaller of two adjacent tanks. If the tanks are spaced at a distance less than B, the differential settlement between the centre and edge could be about 15 percent larger.

Furthermore, the landscaping shall be at least 3 m away from the proposed structure perimeters. A 1.2-m wide concrete or asphalt apron could be constructed adjacent to buildings around the perimeters to protect the foundation soils from surface water and sloped away from the structures to facilitate drainage. Water lines should, if possible, be kept away from the foundations.  In addition, consideration should be given to the use of an impermeable membrane placed around building perimeters to a distance of approximately 1.5 m beyond the edge of the foundations and sloped The hot water systems shall be served from local electrical water heaters, with central storage systems being provided only for large buildings with heavy demand for hot water.
